findings.claim: Deleting deploy/pre-push leaves the documented `.git/hooks/pre-push -> ../../deploy/pre-push` symlink dangling in any clone that installed it, and git then skips the hook without a message until the user also runs `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`.
findings.impact: On the developer's existing clone, pushes that touch frontend/ stop running vitest/tsc/eslint with no warning, so a frontend break reaches CI that the old hook would have caught locally. The check passes silently.
findings.evidence: The commit deletes deploy/pre-push. The old install instruction removed from docs/developer-guide/testing.md was `ln -s ../../deploy/pre-push .git/hooks/pre-push`. The replacement (.githooks/pre-push) runs only once core.hooksPath is set (docs/process/limitations.md: '`core.hooksPath` is per clone'). Nothing in the change removes the old symlink or warns about it.
findings.repro: not_reproduced (read-only reviewer). Expected: in a clone with the old symlink and no core.hooksPath, change a frontend file and run `git push`. No hook output appears and the push goes through.

bucket_proposal.reason: No invariants are declared. This is a one-time migration gap in the user's own clone, not a code path that breaks a declared property.

findings.proposed_fix: Tell the user to run `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` (and remove the stale .git/hooks/pre-push symlink) when this lands, for example in the PR body.

findings.claim: `test_dirs` in process/process.conf includes non-test source trees (`frontend/src`, `mcp-server/src`, `addons`), so check-traceability treats a SPEC-ID that appears anywhere in production source or an addon as a test citation.
findings.impact: An `implemented` ledger row can pass traceability because the ID appears in a source comment or constant, even when no test cites it. The traceability check then passes without a test.
findings.evidence: process/process.conf:9 `test_dirs=backend/tests tests frontend/src ... mcp-server/src ... addons`. In scripts/process/check-traceability.sh, `referenced()` greps those directories recursively with no filter on test file names.
findings.repro: not_reproduced. Expected: add an `implemented` row SPEC-CORE-001 with a valid Approval, put `// SPEC-CORE-001` in a non-test file under frontend/src/, and run check-traceability. It prints `ok`.

bucket_proposal.reason: The ledger is empty today, so no row can be affected yet. The vitest tests are colocated in frontend/src, which makes the directory choice understandable.

specification_compliance: No spec or invariants file exists for this change. It installs the process kit and adapts the project conf. There is no spec to check against.
regression_risks: The new pre-push hook also runs classify-risk, which needs jq and a resolvable origin/develop. A clone without jq will have pushes blocked with 'failed: classification'. That failure is loud, not silent.
The frontend gate decides whether to run from the working tree, including untracked files, not from the pushed commits. This is the same as the old hook.
Setting core.hooksPath to .githooks turns off any other hooks a clone had in .git/hooks.
test_coverage: The change adds no tests for scripts/process-gates/frontend.sh, the gates.conf expect_regex, or the conf values. The expect_regex `^frontend-gate: skipped|Tests +[1-9][0-9]* passed` with NO_COLOR=1 matches vitest's summary line, and a vitest run that collects no tests fails it.
not_verified: The part of review.sh after the 200000-byte truncation, and validate-artifact.sh.
No script was run: precheck, secret-scan, classify-risk, the hook and the workflow were all checked only by reading.
